extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology record; claims are indirect BioSAXS/EM ultrastructural evidence and not promoted to direct target binding.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: 14D and 69D in E. coli UB1005 and MRSA
mechanism_claims.claim_text: BioSAXS and EM showed treatment-associated ultrastructural changes in both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, supporting a broad indirect mode-of-action context for the two D-peptides.
mechanism_claims.limitations: BioSAXS/EM morphology is not direct molecular target identification.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper interprets E. coli nucleoid/cytoplasm separation as similar in direction to ribosome-acting drug responses, but this remains a hypothesis/cell-response comparison rather than direct proof of ribosome or protein-synthesis inhibition.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct ribosome binding, translation inhibition assay, or biochemical target assay is reported for 14D/69D in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper notes that 69D also seems to affect the cellular wall in E. coli while typical dramatic membrane/wall damage was not detected; this is preserved as a cautious morphology observation.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Cell-wall involvement is not resolved to a direct antimicrobial target.

caution_findings.evidence_context: BioSAXS/EM support morphology and cell-response comparisons only; direct mechanism remains unproven.
